title: Detection of vanishing on affine weakly contractible objects
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete ring, let $T$ be a scheme and let
$F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the
small pro-étale site
$T_{\Proet}$.

1. **(i)** $F=0$ if and only if $F(W)=0$ for every affine weakly
contractible object $W\to T$ of $T_{\Proet}$.
1. **(ii)** More generally, a complex of $\Lambda$-module sheaves on
$T_{\Proet}$ is acyclic if and only if its evaluation at every affine
weakly contractible object of $T_{\Proet}$ is an acyclic complex.

Consequently the family of evaluation functors $F\mapsto F(W)$, indexed
by the affine weakly contractible objects, is a detection device on the
whole pro-étale topos, although geometric-point stalks are not
conservative on the pro-étale topos in general, as explained in clause (4) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative].

proof.text: *(i).* The implication from left to right is immediate. Conversely, let $V$ be any object of $T_{\Proet}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family], choose a covering family $\{W_i\to V\}_{i\in I}$ whose members are affine and weakly contractible. The sheaf equalizer axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] gives an injection $F(V)\hookrightarrow\prod_i F(W_i)$. If every $F(W_i)$ is zero, then $F(V)=0$; since $V$ was arbitrary, $F=0$.

source.place: Tag 0990, lemma-proetale-enough-w-contractible, together with the sheaf equalizer axiom

proof.text: Forgetting the left $\Lambda$-action preserves homology and detects zero sheaves: the kernels and sheafified sectionwise cokernels of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] have the same underlying abelian sheaves before and after forgetting the action, and the zero module sheaf has zero underlying abelian sheaf. To apply the commutative-coefficient evaluation theorem, give any abelian sheaf $P$ the sectionwise integer action by repeated addition. Apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface] to the constant ring presheaf $U\mapsto\mathbf Z$ and this presheaf of modules $P$. Its ring sheafification is $\mathbf Z_T$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and its abelian sheafification is canonically $P$ itself since $P$ is already a sheaf. The cited functor therefore equips $P$ with a $\mathbf Z_T$-module structure without changing its sections, and extends every abelian-sheaf morphism (which is sectionwise $\mathbf Z$-linear) without changing its underlying maps. The same kernel and cokernel formulas show that this passage also preserves homology. Thus the subsequent calculation over $\mathbf Z_T$ computes the underlying abelian groups of the original homology sheaves even for noncommutative $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, underlying abelian sheaves; Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules, applied to the constant integer ring presheaf

proof.text: Fix any affine weakly contractible object $W$ of $T_{\Proet}$. Weak contractibility means that every epimorphism of sheaves of sets is surjective on sections over $W$, exactly the definition stated in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact] with $X=T$, $R=\mathbf Z_T$ and this $W$. Its conclusion, together with step 2, gives for every degree $n$ an isomorphism of abelian groups $H^n(K(W))\cong (\mathcal H^n(K))(W)$ for any complex $K$ of left $\Lambda$-module sheaves. Here $K(W)$ means termwise evaluation, and $\mathcal H^n(K)$ is the module-sheaf homology, whose underlying abelian sheaf was identified in step 2. No commutativity of $\Lambda$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0946, lemma-w-contractible (1); Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles, proof of (1)

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], acyclicity is the vanishing of every $\mathcal H^n(K)=\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$. If these sheaves are zero, step 3 makes every $H^n(K(W))$ zero. Conversely, if every evaluated complex $K(W)$ is acyclic, step 3 makes $(\mathcal H^n(K))(W)=0$ for every affine weakly contractible $W$ and every $n$. Clause (i), already proved in step 1, applied to the module sheaf $\mathcal H^n(K)$ then gives $\mathcal H^n(K)=0$. This proves clause (ii), degree by degree, for unbounded complexes as well.

source.place: Tag 0947, proposition-enough-weakly-contractibles (1), applied separately to each three-term segment of the complex

proof.text: Clauses (i) and (ii) give the claimed detection of vanishing and acyclicity. More explicitly, if a sheaf morphism evaluates to an isomorphism at every affine weakly contractible object, its kernel and cokernel have zero evaluations by steps 2 and 3. Clause (i) makes both sheaves zero, so the morphism is an isomorphism in the abelian module category. Thus this evaluation family is jointly conservative on sheaves. The warning compares this with geometric-point stalks: these are not conservative in general for arbitrary pro-étale sheaves, as stated in clause (4) of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative].
